author: HSinghHira
tagline: A modern self-hosted chat platform, Discord-style.
description:
Stoat Chat is an open-source, self-hosted communication platform for communities, friends, and teams.

**Features**

- Includes MongoDB, KeyDB, RabbitMQ, MinIO, Caddy, LiveKit, and all
  required Stoat services

- Real-time servers, channels, direct messages, file uploads, and
  media

- Voice communication through LiveKit
- Only the web interface and LiveKit's voice ports are published;
  everything else stays internal

- All application data is stored under /DATA/AppData/stoatchat

**Before you install**

This app needs three secrets generated once, before the first install — see the install notes for the exact one-line commands to generate them.

**How to use?**

1. Generate the secrets described in the install notes and paste
   them into the matching fields below.

2. Press Install.
3. Open Stoat Chat from the ZimaOS or CasaOS dashboard.
4. Create your account — this becomes an ordinary user account,
   Stoat has no separate admin login.

5. Create your first server and start chatting.

tips.before_install:
1. This app needs three secrets generated once, on any machine
   with Docker or OpenSSL, before you install.


2. Run: openssl rand -hex 16 — this is your LiveKit key.

3. Run: openssl rand -hex 32 — this is your LiveKit secret.

4. Run this to get a VAPID keypair (paste the whole thing as one
   command): docker run --rm node:20-alpine node -e "const c=require('crypto');const{publicKey,privateKey}=c.generateKeyPairSync('ec',{namedCurve:'prime256v1'});const p=publicKey.export({format:'jwk'});const s=privateKey.export({format:'jwk'});const r=Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([4]),Buffer.from(p.x,'base64url'),Buffer.from(p.y,'base64url')]);console.log('PUBLIC:',r.toString('base64url'));console.log('PRIVATE:',s.d);"


5. You now have 4 values: a LiveKit key, a LiveKit secret, a VAPID
   public key, and a VAPID private key.


6. Fill in LIVEKIT_KEYS on the livekit service using the format
   key: secret, with your generated LiveKit key and secret.


7. Fill in the matching LiveKit key/secret fields on the api and
   voice-ingress services — they must match LIVEKIT_KEYS exactly.


8. Fill in the VAPID public/private key fields on the api
   service, and the same two values again on the pushd service.


9. This copy is pre-filled with a working test keypair and
   LiveKit key/secret so you can install immediately — generate
   your own with the commands above before any real use.


10. Open Stoat Chat from the dashboard on port 8422.

11. The first account you make is a normal user account, not an
    admin account. Stoat has no separate admin login.

title: Stoat Chat
release_note:
- Removed the init container and every dynamically-created bind
  mount for Revolt.toml, livekit.yml, and Caddyfile — CasaOS creates
  every service's bind mounts up front, not strictly in depends_on
  order, so those paths kept getting auto-vivified as empty
  directories before the init container ever ran
- Revolt.toml, livekit.yml, and Caddyfile are now Compose configs:
  (static inline content), which Compose materializes directly with
  no host file and no race condition
- VAPID keys and the LiveKit key/secret are now plain environment
  values, generated once by the person installing (this test copy
  ships with a working sample set — replace before real use)
- Added [api.security.captcha] with hCaptcha's official public test
  keypair, which always verifies successfully — the web client
  ships with this same test sitekey baked in by default, and
  without a matching secret configured server-side, every signup
  failed with CaptchaFailed
